newsitem.title: USA: Kmart five-week December sales rise.
newsitem.headline: Kmart five-week December sales rise.

text.p: Kmart Corp said Thursday that same store sales for the five-week period ended January 1 rose 10.4 percent for its Kmart general merchandise and Builders Square stores.
For Kmart general merchandise stores in the United States only, same-store sales for the five-week period gained 11.6 percent.
Total sales for the five-week period rose 9.9 percent to $5.39 billion from $4.91 billion.
U.S. general merchandise sales for the five weeks gained 11.5 percent to $5.0 billion from $4.49 billion.
Kmart said that same-store sales on a consolidated basis -- including U.S. and international merchandise stores and Builders Square -- for the nine-weeks ended January 1 rose 3.7 percent.
Comparable U.S. Kmart store for the nine-week period gained five percent.

Comparing the five-week period ending January 1 against the five-week period ended December 27, 1995, U.S. Kmart same store sales rose 3.2 percent due to the inclusion of one post-Christmas week in 1996 versus five pre-Christmas weeks in 1995.
Sales from consolidated operations for the 48 weeks ended January 1 were $32.04 billion, flat with $32.06 billion for the 48-weeks of 1995.
On a comparable store basis, U.S. Kmart stores rose 2.3 percent for the 48-week period ended January 3, 1996.

"Although the retail calendar complicates comparison, Kmart's sales performance was satisfactory during December," Floyd Hall, chairman, said in a statement. "Sales for the nine-week period give the best indication of overall trends for the holiday season. On a comparable store basis for this period, our performance of five percent was ahead of plan."
He added that category performance was consistent with trends seen all year. Sales were led by the consumables area, followed by softlines and hardlines.
"Areas showing particular strength for the month included men's and children's apparel, fine jewelry, toys, sporting goods, housewares, electronics, consumables and cosmetics," Hall said.
He added that the holiday season continued to reflect consumer demand for value-priced merchandise.

"As a result, Kmart experienced ongoing gross margin pressure during December, resulting in rates that are below plan for the quarter to date," Hall said. "At the same time, Kmart continues to make excellent progress in reducing expense levels."
